title.narrative: The Agriculture Investment and Market Development Project

description.narrative: The development objective of the Agriculture Investment and Market Development Project for Cameroon is to support the transformation of low productivity, subsistence-oriented cassava, maize, and sorghum sub-sectors into commercially-oriented and competitive value chains in four agro-ecological areas. The project has three components. The first component, support to agricultural production, processing, and marketing aim to establish productive partnerships (PPs) between producer organizations (POs) and agri-business (ABs) that will lead to increased productivity, production, and quality of the identified value chains. The component is organized under four sub-components: (i) establishing of PPs; (ii) financing of sub-project (SPs) for POs; (iii) financing of basic public infrastructure; and (iv) supporting improved access to rural financing. The second component, support to seed production and distribution system, relevant public services, and technology transfer will support the implementation of first component by: (a) strengthening the seed system and the capacity of public services key to the project; (b) creating a framework for cooperation between the Government of Cameroon (GOC), POs, ABs, financial institution (FIs), and other actors that will play an important role in the project; and (c) enhancing agricultural technology transfers. It comprises three sub-components: (i) enhancement of the seed production and distribution systems? relevant public services; (ii) building a commodity-based public-private consultation and partnership framework; and (iii) enhancement of agricultural technology transfers and promotion of healthy food and nutrition practices. The third component, project coordination and management objective is to: (a) ensure effective strategic and operational planning, monitoring, and implementation of the project and efficient coordination between first and second components and the various sources of funding and project implementation partners; (b) evaluate the project?s final results and impact on smallholders and POs; and (c) communicate efficiently to various public entities on project activities, outcomes, and lessons learnt. The component has two sub-components: (i) strategic planning, coordination, management, and implementation support; and (ii) monitoring and evaluation, communication, and knowledge production and sharing.
To support the transformation of low productivity, subsistence-oriented cassava, maize and sorghum sub-sectors into commercially-oriented and competitive value chains in four agro-ecological areas.

title.narrative: Increased quality as measured by price premium of produce sold by beneficiary farmers in the targeted value chains

comment.narrative: <p>Maize quality as measured by price premium achieved by beneficiaries exceed target: 114.6 percent. Sorghum falls short of meeting the target by 14.3 percent. For cassava, at closing, the cooperatives were still at the start of delivery. The initial prices for maize and sorghum were XAF 133,800 and 175,000 per ton respectively. The average unit prices negotiated with ABs were XAF 156,808 and 205,000 per ton generating price premia 17.2 and 17.14 percent for maize and sorghum respectively. Delays in delivery for ccassavastems from the fact the initial AIMDP model was incompatible with private sector<strong>.</strong> In the PAD beneficiary cooperatives in the cassava value chain were expected to process cassava and supply starch to NCSA. The later, requested convincing proof of production capacity (in terms of land, infrastructure, and human resource) before signing the purchase agreement. In addition, for NCSA the actual contract was conditional to meeting the quality standard audited by its own experts. This risk management strategy of NCSA was incompatible with the AIMDP partnership scheme of AIMDP in which deals were expected to be made before installation of starch processing facilities. Later, NCSA decided to drop purchasing the starch. At the same time small and processing units recorded delays in equipment acquisitions.</p>

title.narrative: Increase yield of targeted crops by direct beneficiaries

comment.narrative: <p>The Project achieved 89, 96, and 89 percent of targets for maize, sorghum, cassava respectively. The targets were 267, 200, and 300 percent increase over baseline averages of 1.5, 1, 8 MT/ha for maize, sorghum, and cassava respectively. The actual yields achieved represented increases of 237 percent, 191 percent, and 279 percent for maize, sorghum, and cassava respectively.  This indicator is linked to the support to the seed production and distribution system, relevant public services and to technology transfer. While crop yields in all three-value chain significantly increased compare to the baseline, they all failed to meet the targets. This is due to several factors: (i) including reduction in costs of activities supporting technologies transfer; (ii) Inadequacy of certain varieties of maize seeds distributed; (ii) unpredictable weather in the North and the Far North region; (iii) security crises in the North West and the South West.</p>

<p>The PAD proposed to establish a commodity-based public-private consultation platform as a permanent institution to promote valued chain development of target commodities. A platform was set up on April 13, 2015 by Ministerial decision N° 0711/CAB/MINADER/ and launched on September 17, 2015 (100% completion rate). The technical coordinators and secretaries of the four committees were elected in 2018 and the committees submitted roadmaps for the implementation of their action plan included in the AWPB. Although the initiative to create the platform was positively appreciated by stakeholders, the effects (implementation of information systemson the market, resolution of conflicts discussed or resolved, etc.) envisioned by its creation were not yet visible at closing.</p>

title.narrative: Post-harvest or processing facilities constructed or rehabilitated

comment.narrative: <p>The target was exceeded: 115 percent.  At PAD the target was set at 160 Post-harvest or processing facilities. The 2019 restructuring revised the target down to 100. At closing 115 Post-harvest or processing facilities were constructed or rehabilitated.</p>

Clients who have adopted an improved agr. technology promoted by the project

comment.narrative: <p>The Project achieved 67 percent of the target. At PDA the target was set at 120,000 beneficiaries. The target was adjusted down to 25,000 during the February 2018 restructuring. At closing the number of beneficiaries who have adopted improved agriculture technologies promoted by the project was 16,752</p>

<p>Certified seeds produced and distributed achieved 45, 14, 83, and 10 percent of the end of Project targets for maize, sorghum, cassava cuttings, and bio-fortified cassava respectively. The PAD targets were 3700, 3800, 80000000, and 5000000 metric ton respectively. After restructuring these targets were revised to 4400, 1000, 20890000, and 1709000 respectively. At the end of the Project, only 1977, 137, 17394000, and 169500 of certified seeds were produced and distributed for maize, sorghum, cassava cuttings, and bio-fortified cassava respectively. This low level of achievement is explained by the fact that production activities of eligible sorghum seed cooperatives (registered, having adopted business plans, having mobilized their 10%) to co-financing of PIDMA started quite late (year 2020), particularly for maize and sorghum.</p>

<p>The target was exceeded: 126 percent. The PAD target was 120,000 beneficiaries. The target was revised up during the 2019 restructuring to 140,000 beneficiaries. At closing 176,254 people had benefited from the Project, of which Female beneficiaries were 36 percent compared to the target of 70 percent (51 percent).</p>

<p>The achievement against the end of Project target was 100 percent. The PAD target was 35 PPs. The 2018 restructuring adjusted down the target to 20. At the end of the Project 20 PPs were established. Despite a 100 percent not all the PPs were functioning as intended.</p>

<p>The target was exceeded: 114 percent. At PAD the target was set at 500 km of rural roads rehabilitated. The 2018 restructuring revised the target down to 193. The 2019 restructuring adjusted the target to 190 km. At closing 217 farms had adopted bio-fortified varieties. There was however a substantial sustainability risk as the committees set up by the Project for maintenance of infrastructures were still nascent with limited resources.</p>

<p>The achievement against the end of Project target was 78 percent. The PAD target was 300 SPs. The 2018 restructuring adjusted down the target to 100. At the end of the Project 78 SPs were established.</p>

title.narrative: Women who benefited from labor-saving technologies and equipment

comment.narrative: <p>At closing Achievement against target was about 35 percent. The PAD target was 84000 women beneficiaries. After the 2018 restructuring the target was set to 25000. At the end of the Project only 8735 women had benefited from labor-saving technologies and equipment.</p>

comment.narrative: <p>Foundation seeds produced and distributed achieved 92, 38, 101, and 78 percent of the end of project targets for maize, sorghum,cassava cuttings, and bio-fortified cassava respectively. At PAD the targets were 130, 130, 9000000, and 735000 metric ton respectively. During the February 2018 restructuring the targets for maize, sorghum, cassava cutting, and bio-fortified cassava were adjusted to 176, 205, 4680000, and 550000 respectively. The June 2019 adjusted the target for cassava cutting to 8900000.</p>

title.narrative: Farms that have adopted bio-fortified varieties

comment.narrative: <p>The target was exceeded: 106 percent. At PAD the target was set at 6000 beneficiaries. The 2018 restructuring revised the targetdown to 310. The 2019 restructuring adjusted the target to 900 beneficiaries. At closing 958 farms had adopted bio-fortified varieties.</p>

title.narrative: Farms that have adopted bio-fortified varieties
Agro-Business buyers' rate of satisfaction on achievement of contractual commitments of cooperatives for selected commodities

comment.narrative: <p>Achievements against targets were 92, 89, and 29 percent for maize, sorghum, and cassava respectively. This indicator was added during the 2018 restructuring to remeasure satisfaction of effectiveness of implementation of contractual arrangements between producers and buyers. For maize and sorghum, the satisfaction rates improved significantly once the productive investment such as drying, and storage units were put in place. Acquisition of processing unit for maize recorded extended delays.    </p>

title.narrative: Increased volume of targeted crops sold by participating cooperatives to buyers from productive partnerships (Agro-Business)

comment.narrative: <p>An increase in volume marketed indicator was added during the February 2018 restructuring to measure the effectiveness of the contractual arrangements among those participating. The initial outcome targets set for this indicator were 65,700, 10,600, and 14,400metric ton for maize, sorghum, and cassava respectively. During the June 2019 restructuring, the outcome targets for maize and cassava were revised down to 25,000 and 5,000 metric ton respectively. Beneficiary cooperative marketed 114.3, 132.0, and 89.0 percent of the revised targets for maize, sorghum, and cassava, respectively. Cassava marketing failed to meet target because many of the purchase contracts for cassava failed.</p>

Rate of credit reimbursement of participating cooperatives to partner Financial Institutions (IFPs)

comment.narrative: <p>The target was exceeded: 108 percent. This indicator was added during the 2018 restructuring to measure the effectiveness of FIs’ credit mechanism for cooperatives. The PDA target was 75 percent. The Project achieved 81 percent.  The end of Project impact study revealed that for IFPs outside the partnership with AIMDP, the repayment rate of loans intended for agriculture is around 60 percent on average.</p>

comment.narrative: <p>At closing the GRM was operational, with a total 165 complaints registered. 122 complaints were related to road works, 10 to micro-projects, 32 to activities related to Nutrition, and 1 complaint related to procurement. At the end of the Project, 159 complaints out of the 165 were closed. The unresolved complaints were related to rural roads not completed at closing.   </p>
